title: Exercise in daylight
summary: Walking, resistance bands, or rebounding—indoors or outdoors—with duration practiced as Exercise, preferably stacked with real daylight.

sections.heading: Movement plus light
sections.body: Exercise in outdoor light couples muscle pump, lymph flow, and melanopsin drive—usually a better mitochondrial-lifestyle default than only treadmill-under-fluorescents. The habit is not “morning only forever”; it is regular mechanical load with a bias toward daylight when your schedule allows.

sections.heading: What you can practice
sections.body: Under Exercise, pick rebounding, resistance bands, or walking; choose outdoors or indoors; then session length. Outdoor movement may provide a stronger outdoor-light signal in this guide. Rebounding needs a stable rebounder—see the lymphatic rebounding lesson. Bands and walking need little gear. Nature immersion covers longer green/blue hangs that are not primarily “workout” shaped.

sections.heading: Practical habit
sections.body: Start with a duration you will repeat: a brisk outdoor walk after morning light, a short rebound session, or a band circuit on a porch. Build load gradually. Pair hard sessions with food, minerals, and sleep—not with chronic under-recovery papered over by more volume. Indoor movement remains useful on bad weather days; keep chasing outdoor light as the preference, not a purity test.

sections.heading: Where Dr. Jack Kruse’s teaching is specific
sections.body: Kruse ties exercise to circadian and light context: train under sun when possible, avoid living as a nocturnal gym-only organism, and nest movement inside the light–water–magnetism stack (including cold and grounding). Exact sport prescriptions vary in his material; the durable teaching is daylight + muscle use + recovery environment.

sections.heading: What is solid, what is framework
sections.body: Solid ground: skeletal muscle activity moves lymph and supports metabolic health; outdoor light anchors circadian timing; progressive overload beats random hero days. Framework: that only one modality (e.g. rebounding) is uniquely mitochondrial. Use any mode you will sustain.

sections.heading: How to use it here
sections.body: Practice Exercise with mode, environment, and duration. Add Nature immersion for non-workout outdoor blocks; Grounding when skin-to-earth is intentional. Read Rebounding and the lymphatic system if you own a rebounder. Educational only.
